editorial.marketOverview: US cash markets have not reopened since Friday November 20. Reuters reported Nasdaq Composite -5.28% and SOX roughly -11%; secondary QQQ reporting indicated -5.67%, while Barron's reported VIX 37.66 at Friday's close. The unusually large semiconductor underperformance, negative breadth and elevated protection demand sustain a bearish near-term skew, but none of these is a live Sunday quote.
editorial.whatChanged: Compared with the Saturday 23:35 EST snapshot, the Sunday review found no verified new US session, no updated curated Open Watch event and no incremental catalyst that changes the three-session path. MarketWatch's reported Friday SOX -10.7% and $2.3 trillion weekly chip-sector wipeout further characterize already-known losses, rather than a new event. November 23–25 scheduled releases remain future risks.
editorial.marketInterpretation: The combination of semiconductor leadership failure, broad risk reduction and elevated volatility favors defensive positioning into the reopening. A sharp oversold rebound is possible, so price confirmation after the Monday open is essential. Nvidia regulatory reporting is an investigation, not a finding of wrongdoing; anticipated PMI, PCE and earnings effects are scenarios rather than observed reactions. A stale 29bp 10Y–2Y proxy must not be treated as synchronized rates data.
editorial.threeDayPath: Monday November 23: watch opening gaps, whether SOX/SMH lead or lag QQQ, breadth and volatility after 09:45 ET flash PMIs. Tuesday November 24: assess follow-through versus failed rebound around consumer confidence and ADI/Dell earnings. Wednesday November 25: elevated two-way gap risk around the 08:30 ET PCE, GDP, durable-goods and claims cluster, followed by 14:00 ET Beige Book. Bearish base case persists unless breadth and semiconductor leadership recover together.
editorial.bullCase: Extreme Friday losses create potential for short-covering, especially if yields ease, inflation expectations cool and semiconductors stabilize. A credible bullish revision requires QQQ and SOX/SMH to advance together, broader participation, and a sustained decline in VXN/VIX rather than a single opening bounce.
editorial.bearCase: Friday's semiconductor capitulation and Nvidia-related uncertainty could extend into Monday, especially if SOX continues to lag, advance-decline measures remain weak and volatility stays elevated. Hawkish Fed repricing or an upside inflation surprise Wednesday would amplify duration-sensitive Nasdaq pressure; these are unobserved conditional outcomes.
